outcome_detail: Federal suit (Terrell v. Harris County, No. 4:22-cv-00302, S.D. Tex., filed January 30, 2022) dismissed by the district court for failure to state a claim: qualified immunity for Deputy Mark Cannon, and insufficient pattern allegations for supervisory liability against Sheriff Ed Gonzalez and municipal liability against Harris County; the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed Deputy Michael Hines. The Fifth Circuit affirmed on July 9, 2024 (No. 23-20281). A separate state-court suit against the bar where the deputies worked security reportedly ended in a confidential settlement.
criminal_detail: Michael Jarell Hines pleaded guilty to attempted sexual assault and on June 26, 2023 received six years of deferred adjudication (probation) with no jail time; he must register as a sex offender for 10 years and cannot possess firearms. Earlier reporting (February 2022) said Hines had a prior criminal charge involving a child.
description: A woman sued Harris County, Sheriff Ed Gonzalez, and deputies Michael Jarell Hines and Mark Cannon in federal court in January 2022 under 42 U.S.C. Section 1983 (Terrell v. Harris County, No. 4:22-cv-00302, S.D. Tex.). According to the complaint, after she drank at a Houston bar in February 2020 where the deputies were working off-duty security in their uniforms with patrol vehicles, the deputies placed her in a patrol car rather than allowing her to go home; she said she did not remember what followed and awoke the next morning with injuries, and a rape kit identified Hines' DNA on her undergarment. Hines pleaded guilty to attempted sexual assault and in June 2023 received six years of deferred adjudication probation with sex-offender registration. The district court dismissed the claims against Cannon (qualified immunity), Gonzalez, and Harris County for failure to state a claim, the plaintiff voluntarily dismissed Hines, and the Fifth Circuit affirmed the dismissal on July 9, 2024. Her attorney said a separate state-court suit against the bar was resolved through a confidential settlement.
notes: Outside strict police-department definition (sheriff). A related state-court suit against The Address bar (a private venue, not a law-enforcement defendant) reportedly settled confidentially; it is noted here rather than recorded as a companion lawsuit because no law-enforcement defendant was reported in that action.
